extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities, comprising 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.publisher: CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 source datasets. Text instructions were synthesized into speech using TTS models. A multi-stage curation process was applied including deduplication, validation, categorization, and balanced sampling.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data extracted from 37 datasets including LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, AudioCaps, AVQA, MusicCaps, MUSICA VQA, SUPERB, HEAR, AIR-Bench, MMMU, and others.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were rewritten for TTS suitability. Special tokens were replaced with descriptive phrases. Multiple-choice options were rephrased for readability. Audio was synthesized and transcribed back to text to verify quality via Word Error Rate.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was used: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance; (2) Validation to exclude incomplete, corrupted, or ill-posed items; (3) Categorization into 13 task categories; (4) Balanced sampling to equalize category representation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reference answers were provided from source datasets. For role-play tasks, role profiles and question texts were used. Speech quality was evaluated using UTMOS. Content quality was assessed using gpt-oss-20b with specific evaluator prompts. Consistency was measured using modified Word Error Rate (WER) between transcribed speech and text responses.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validation was conducted on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B's outputs, showing strong agreement (96.1% overall) and high correlation (0.92) with automated GPT-based scoring.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: F5TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B (TTS models), UTMOS Strong (speech quality), Whisper-Large-v3 (transcription), gpt-oss-20b (content evaluation), emotion2vec (emotion analysis), Wespeaker (speaker similarity)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code will be released publicly. The authors bear responsibility for rights violations and maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes role-play voice imitation tasks which may involve speaker timbre and voice personalization. Safeguards are in place to prevent identity spoofing and harassment.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to evaluate and guide the development of next-generation AI assistants, particularly in healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive industries. It highlights gaps in robustness and safety alignment.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is monolingual (English), which may not capture full variability of real user interactions. Role-play roles are fixed and may encode stereotypes. Source data is drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited diversity in languages (English only). Limited model evaluation scope (mostly open-source, one proprietary). Evaluation relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring which may introduce noise. Lacks video-audio integration and continuous streaming tasks. Does not measure latency, barge-in, or error recovery.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating AI assistants' listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. Testing model robustness, safety alignment, and multimodal integration. Not intended for training models for cheating.
